Greece — Budget breakdown

STAYS

Our four nights cost $435, with the beautiful Anafi suite in Santorini accounting for $135 per night (which by the way, is par for the course in the Aegean islands).

Athens was much cheaper at $82 a night in a residential building only 10 minutes from the Acropolis.

FOOD

Gyros at local legend Kostas in Athens cost $3, whereas the rolls at Istanbul’s equivalent, Durumzade, cost twice as much.

Even the fanciest lunch we had in Santorini (at Melitini) was about $70 for two.

EXPERIENCES

Our mythology tour of ancient Athens was $65 per person plus a $20 tip. Additionally, we paid $50 each for entrance to the Acropolis and the Agora.

Unfortunately, we were underwhelmed by the tour. We’d mention the tour operator, but those details aren’t mentioned on our receipts!

INTER-CITY TRAVELS

We forked out $365 to Volotea airlines, including an unnecessary $60 fine, for the honour of flying us to Santorini.

It’s mostly low-cost airlines operating this route, so if you’re not pressed for time, take the boat.

MISCELLANEOUS

Our visas cost about $90 each. We spent in the range of $20 on moving around the island of Santorini. We walked all across Athens.
